A05-D01 | Party-name decision

OCR of redacted facsimile; layout and embedded images are not reproduced.

[Source page 1]

Unit 
 The Election Unit

Dato
26-04-2022

Ministry of the Interior and 
 Housing

The Election Committee

Application for approval of the party name "The Synthetic
 Party" for participation in parliamentary elections

You have by e-mail of 27 March 2022 applied to the Election Committee to have the name "The Synte-
thetic Party" approved as the name of a new party to participate in upcoming parliamentary elections.

The Election Board hereby approves "The Synthetic Party" as the name of a new party for participation in the upcoming parliamentary election.


The announced approval of the party name is valid for three years counted from today's date, i.e. until
and with that 26 April 2025. Any possible party registration must therefore be submitted to before-
the Minister of the Interior and Housing no later than three years from today's date, i.e. no later than the 26. April 2025.

If you wish to apply for extension of the approval
of the party name at the expiry of the approval period, the application must be submitted no later than the expiry
of the previously granted approval. If you submit an application for extension of the approval
of the party name digitally, an application received on a Saturday, Sunday or
public holiday or submitted after office hours will be considered submitted on that
day. If you submit an application for extension of the approval of the party name
by ordinary mail, an application received on a Saturday, Sunday or
public holiday or submitted after office hours will only be considered received on the
next weekday which is not a Saturday. Furthermore, you should be aware that an
extension of the approval can only be for one year and only if there is reason to believe
that a party notification will be made within one year before the expiry of the extension period.

The granted approval of the party name is given to you personally, who hereby represents 
 the party before the Election Committee and the Ministry of the Interior and Housing. If the approval 
 is transferred to another person or association, the Election Committee must be informed thereof.

Legal basis for the decision 
 The rules concerning the registration of parties wishing to participate in parliamentary elections are found 
 in section 12 of the Parliamentary Election Act (consolidated act no. 294 of 7 March 2022).

New parties that wish to participate in parliamentary elections must be registered with the Ministry of the Interior and Housing
the minister of the interior no later than 12 fifteen days before election day. The notification must be accompanied by a
Clearance from a number of voters at least corresponding to 1/175 of all valid votes
at the most recent parliamentary election. The declarations, which must follow the notification, must
were registered as declarations of support for the party in the digital solution, which interior-
and the housing minister makes himself available to the voters, cf. the Parliamentary Election Act § 12, subsection 1.


[Source page 2]

Before a new party begins collecting voter declarations, the party's name must be approved
recognized by the Election Board, cf. the Parliamentary Election Act § 12, subsection 2 and 3. The detailed rules on
approval of party names is established in the Parliamentary Election Act § 13.

Collection of voter declarations and procedure for party registration

When a new party, which wishes to participate in upcoming parliamentary elections, registers the party
notification to the Minister of the Interior and Housing, the report shall, as stated above, be followed by
declarations from a number of voters corresponding to at least 1/175 of all valid votes
at the most recent parliamentary election (currently 20.182).

The actual collection of voter declarations shall be conducted through the digital voter declaration portal, which the Ministry of the Interior and Housing makes available on the website voter declaration.dk. Immediately after the Election Board's approval of a new party name, the Ministry of the Interior and Housing sets up a collection for the party in the voter declaration portal. Thereafter, anyone with the right to vote in the Folketing can submit a voter declaration for the party. On the portal, the party will appear in a consolidated overview of all parties, where voters can find the party they wish to support. Furthermore, the party can via its own website, social media, email invitations, etc., link directly to the party's collection on the portal.









The party can regularly check the number of valid voter declarations via the voter declaration portal
. When the party has obtained the required number of voter declarations, it can
register with the Minister of the Interior and Housing by submitting a written request to
the Ministry of the Interior and Housing. It is the party's responsibility to document that at the time
of the registration it had the required number of voter declarations, e.g., by means of a screenshot of the party's collection of voter declarations on the portal
.

Collection of voter declarations must be carried out according to the described procedure. In case of 
serious or repeated legal violations in connection with a party's collection of voter declarations
, the Election Board can make a decision to exclude the party from continuing to collect voter declarations and cancel the party's collection.


For more information on the collection and submission of voter declarations, see the page 
 "More on voter declarations" at velgererklering.dk.
